primitives.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Building on this foundation, this paper introduces GridMind, a multi-agent framework that unifies structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and large language models (LLMs) to facilitate natural language querying of NFL data.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$p(w|c)$': 'Generated word probability given context (dimensionless)', '$w$': 'Word token', '$c$': 'Query context', '$D$': 'Retrieved document set', '$p(w|d)$': 'Word likelihood under document distribution (dimensionless)', '$p(d|c)$': 'Document relevance score (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Documents are independent, query distribution matches training data, and embedding spaces are stationary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Information bottleneck when retrieved documents contain conflicting information, leading to hallucination.

primitives.verbatim_quote: cross-modal systems to enhance data interpretation and real-time decision-making in sports and beyond.

primitives.assumptions: Data manifold is locally linear, positive pairs are informative, and batch normalization stabilizes gradients.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is aligning disparate NFL data streams (statistics, telemetry, narratives) into a shared latent space. Multimodal Embedding Alignment achieves this by projecting each modality onto a common Euclidean manifold using learned functions f_m. However, this induces a dual failure mode: when modalities diverge (e.g., statistical anomalies vs. narrative shifts), the embedding becomes non-invertible, creating a singularity where information flows bidirectionally but cannot be uniquely decoded. To mitigate this, we enforce a Lipschitz constraint on f_m, ensuring local injectivity and preventing catastrophic forgetting during continual learning.
